paper.title: Best Arm Identification with Safety Constraints

unmapped: Learner picks coordinate i in [d] and dose a in [a_{0,i}, M_i]; observes y = a*theta_i + noise and safety signal z = a*mu_i + noise (two-dimensional observation)
Safety constraint a*mu_i <= gamma must hold w.p. 1-delta for all pulls; mu, theta unknown and nonnegative
The learner knows the safety threshold gamma, safe initial doses a_{0,i} and bounds M_i
Goal: identify coordinate with largest maximum safe value; gap Delta_i defined via min{gamma*theta_i/mu_i, theta_i*M_i}
settings.definition_quote: at every time step $t$, the learner chooses a coordinate $i_t \in [d]$ and a value $a_t \in [a_{0,i_t}, M_{i_t}]$, and observes y_t = a_t \theta_{i_t} + \eta_t, z_t = a_t \mu_{i_t} + w_t for $\eta_t$ and $w_t$ both $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian ... the learner must always choose, with high probability, $a_t$ and $i_t$ satisfying $a_t \mu_{i_t} \le \gamma$

settings.name_in_paper: Safe best-arm identification, linear response (lower bound)
unmapped: Coordinate-plus-dose actions with linear reward a*theta_i and linear safety a*mu_i, two-dimensional Gaussian observations
Learner is given the set of safe doses S_i by an oracle (may pull any safe dose at any time)
settings.definition_quote: For simplicity, we assume here that $\sigma^2 = 1$ and that $\eta_t \sim \calN(0,\sigma^2), w_t \sim \calN(0,\sigma^2)$. ... we give the algorithm a set of arms it can pull throughout execution.

unmapped: d coordinates, each with a real-valued dose a; observe y = f_i(a)+noise and safety signal z = g_i(a)+noise
f_i nondecreasing with values in [0,1]; g_i 1-Lipschitz and strictly increasing (monotonic response)
Learner may query doses with g_i(a) <= gamma + eps_safe but target is best coordinate under g_i(a) <= gamma
The learner knows gamma, initial safe doses a_{0,i}, and chooses eps_safe
settings.definition_quote: y_t = f_{i_t}(a_t) + \eta_t, z_t = g_{i_t}(a_t) + w_t ... For all $i\in [d]$, $g_i(\cdot)$ is 1-Lipschitz and strictly monotonically increasing. Furthermore, for all $i \in [d]$ and $a \in \bbR$, $f_i(a) \in [0,1]$ and $f_i(\cdot)$ is nondecreasing.

symbols.rho_i: theta_i/mu_i, ratio of reward slope to safety slope of coordinate i

conditions: any (delta, {S_i(mu,gamma)})-PAC algorithm (delta-PAC and only chooses values in the given safe sets)

source.label: thm:linear_lb
source.quote: Fix an instance $\theta \in \bbR_+^d$ and $\mu \in \bbR_+^d$, $\gamma > 0$, and $M_i = \infty$ for all $i$ ... Let $\tau$ denote the stopping time for any $(\delta,\{ \safe_i(\mu,\gamma) \}_{i \in [d]})$-PAC algorithm. Then on this instance we will have that \Exp_{\theta,\mu}[\tau] \ge \frac{2}{3} \log \frac{1}{2.4 \delta} \cdot \sum_{i \neq \ist} \frac{ 1 + \theta_{\ist}^2/\mu_{\ist}^2 + \theta_i^2/\mu_i^2}{\Delta_i^2} .

results.notes: Delta_i is the paper's gap in maximum safe value (gamma*(theta_{i*}/mu_{i*} - theta_i/mu_i) here). Paper's mu_i is the safety slope, not a mean reward.

symbols.N_c_i: case-dependent complexity N_{c(i),i} of coordinate i (four cases depending on whether M_i and M_{i*} are safe), e.g. Case 1: (1+theta_{i*}^2/mu_{i*}^2+theta_i^2/mu_i^2)/Delta_i^2 + C_gamma*max{xi_4(1/(a_{0,i}mu_i)), xi_4(1/(a_{0,i*}mu_{i*}))}

conditions: a_{0,i} mu_i <= gamma for all i

source.label: thm:linear_complexity2_simp
source.quote: Let $\case(i) \in \{1,2,3,4\}$ denote the case coordinate $i$ falls in. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, \Cref{alg:constrained_bai} will output $\ist$, only pull safe arms, and terminate after collecting at most \cOtil ( \log \tfrac{d}{\delta} \cdot \sum_{i \neq \ist} N_{\case(i),i} + \log \tfrac{d}{\delta} \cdot \tfrac{d}{\gamma^8} ) samples.

results.notes: Case-wise N terms compressed into a declared symbol. Full version (Theorem 4) gives the same structure with the 1/gamma^8 term inside each N_{c(i),i}. C_gamma = xi_{sqrt32}(2 gamma), xi_a(x)=2^{a sqrt(log2 max{x,2})}.

bound.expression: log(d/delta)*sum_subopt((1 + rho_star**2 + rho_i**2)/Delta_i**2) + log(d/delta)*sum_subopt(Max(1/gamma_s**8, C_gamma*xi_i, C_gamma*xi_star))

symbols.C_gamma: xi_{sqrt(32)}(2 gamma), with xi_a(x) = 2^{a sqrt(log2 max{x,2})}

conditions: M_i is unsafe for all i
a_{0,i} mu_i <= gamma for all i

source.label: cor:linear_simplified
source.quote: Assume that $M_i$ is unsafe for all $i$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, \Cref{alg:constrained_bai} will output $\ist$, only pull safe arms, and terminate after collecting at most \cOtil (...) samples.

results.notes: Matches the Theorem 1 lower bound up to constants and lower-order terms in a_{0,i} and gamma.

symbols.S_i: sum_{l=1}^{lbar(i)} (mbar_{i,l} + nbar_{i,l} + l + 2) 2^{2l}, with lbar(i), mbar, nbar defined via the inverse safety function g_i^{-1}

conditions: Assumption 1: g_i 1-Lipschitz and strictly increasing; f_i nondecreasing in [0,1]
Assumption 2: g_i^{-1}(x) well defined for x in [gamma, gamma+eps_safe]
tuning: safety slack eps_safe > 0 chosen by user

source.label: thm:monotonic_complexity
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{asm:smooth_fun} and \ref{asm:inverse}, with probability $1-\delta$, \Cref{alg:constrained_bai_monotonic2} will terminate and output $\ist$ after collecting at most \cOtil ( \log \tfrac{1}{\delta} \cdot \sum_{i = 1, i \neq \ist}^d \sum_{\ell = 1}^{\ellbar(i) } ( \mbar_{i,\ell} + \nbar_{i,\ell} + \ell + 2 ) 2^{2 \ell} ) samples, and will only pull safe arms during execution.

results.notes: Full version is Theorem 5 in appendix. 'Safe' here means g_i(a) <= gamma + eps_safe is allowed per the query model, though the statement says only safe arms are pulled.

symbols.L_g: constant L with g_i'(a) >= 1/L on the relevant interval (Assumption 3)
symbols.ginv_i: g_i^{-1}(gamma), largest safe dose of coordinate i

conditions: Assumption 3: g_i differentiable, g_i^{-1} defined on [gamma-3/2, gamma+eps_safe], g_i'(a) >= 1/L there (L unknown to learner)

source.label: cor:mon_simplified_complexity
source.quote: Assume that Assumption \ref{asm:cont_deriv} holds. Then, with probability $1-\delta$, \Cref{alg:constrained_bai_monotonic2} will terminate and output $\ist$ after collecting at most \cOtil (...) samples, and will only pull safe arms during execution.

results.notes: Delta_i is the gap in maximum safe reward f_i(g_i^{-1}(gamma)).
